implementation_summary: server.ts: added exported read-only interface AuditWiring {dataDir, store, keys, helperAccess, readAiModels(), isOwnerRequest(req)} and public getter RunnerServer.auditWiring returning one frozen object per runner. The constructor builds exactly one audit store, createAuditStore(selectAuditStoreBackend({ dataDir })), and a HelperAccess over that same store, createHelperAccess({ ...helperSettingsFromEnv(), accessToken: this.accessToken, store }), so Helper sign-in follows the runner's own key (DEC-004). Dispatch uses options.helperAccess, else the runner's own Helper access only when enabled; helperGrants keeps its precedence (option, then the Helper access hook). The wiring always carries a Helper access (disabled when Helper sign-in is not set up) so the Helper rows can say it is not set up. readAiModels exposes only provider, text and vision. Private members are unchanged, so BE-190's current cast keeps working until it switches to auditWiring. cli.ts was not changed because the server reads the Helper settings from the environment itself.

risks: RunnerServer now builds the audit store backend in its constructor: an invalid AUDIT_STORE_BUCKET throws there and the runner does not start (fail-fast). Before, only the audit routes failed.

Helper access is now live in dispatch on the deployed beta copy (deploy sets RUNNER_BETA=1 and FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID). authorizeRoute already serves Helper-granted rows in beta; the beta rules are unchanged. A reviewer should confirm this is intended.
The runner's own Helper access takes this.accessToken (options) instead of env RUNNER_ACCESS_TOKEN. In cli.ts they are the same value; a runner built in code without a key keeps Helper sign-in off.
Until BE-190 switches to auditWiring, routes/index.ts builds a second AuditStore on the same folder, so per-instance audit locks are not shared between the routes and Helper access.
